message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep completed for the monitored products in Products.txt, covering the last 24 hours ending with the scheduled run on 2026-06-19 05:10 IST. Confirmed relevant findings were found for Node.js, Microsoft Edge, Ubuntu, Apache Tomcat via Ubuntu packaging, and Google Chrome/Chromium browser exposure. MongoDB-related items with fresh enrichment or secondary coverage are listed separately as possible matches needing review because the underlying CVEs appear to have been published earlier than this 24-hour window.

**Finding 1: Node.js June 2026 security releases**

- Product: Node.js
- Issue: Multiple Node.js CVEs fixed across supported 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines, including CVE-2026-48933, CVE-2026-48618, CVE-2026-48615, CVE-2026-48619, CVE-2026-48937, CVE-2026-48928, CVE-2026-48930, CVE-2026-48934, CVE-2026-48935, CVE-2026-48936, and CVE-2026-48931.
- Severity: Highest stated severity is High.
- Description: The Node.js project released supported-line updates addressing denial-of-service, TLS/hostname verification, proxy credential leakage, permission-model bypass, HTTP/2 cleanup, and response-queue poisoning issues.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list explicitly includes Node.js, and the advisory is from the Node.js project.
- Source: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/june-2026-security-releases

**Finding 2: Microsoft Edge Stable update with Chromium security fixes**

- Product: Microsoft Edge
- Issue: Microsoft Edge Stable 149.0.4022.80.
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Microsoft for the June 18 Edge entry; Microsoft says CVEs will be added as available.
- Description: Microsoft released an Edge Stable update on June 18, 2026 that incorporates the latest Chromium project security updates.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list explicitly includes Microsoft Edge, and Microsoft names Edge Stable directly. The exact CVE mapping for the June 18 Edge update had not yet been published on the Microsoft release-notes page at review time.
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Finding 3: Ubuntu / Apache Tomcat package security update**

- Product: Ubuntu and Apache Tomcat
- Issue: USN-8450-1 covering CVE-2026-41284, CVE-2026-41293, CVE-2026-42498, and CVE-2026-43515 in Tomcat.
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice.
- Description: Canonical fixed Tomcat issues that could allow denial of service, possible arbitrary code execution, credential exposure during WebSocket upgrades/redirects, or authorization bypass.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes both Ubuntu and Apache Tomcat; the Ubuntu notice names the tomcat11 package directly.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8450-1

**Finding 4: Ubuntu libheif security update**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: USN-8454-1 covering multiple libheif CVEs, including CVE-2026-32738, CVE-2026-32739, CVE-2026-32740, CVE-2026-32741, CVE-2026-32814, CVE-2026-32882, CVE-2026-3950, CVE-2026-41069, and CVE-2026-41071.
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice.
- Description: Canonical fixed multiple malformed HEIF/AVIF image handling issues that could cause denial of service, information disclosure, or arbitrary code execution depending on release and package use.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Ubuntu, and this is an official Ubuntu Security Notice affecting supported Ubuntu releases.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8454-1

**Finding 5: Ubuntu access-control and resolver-related package updates**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: USN-8453-1 for Net::CIDR::Lite, USN-8452-1 for pbkdf2, and USN-8449-1 for ldns.
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notices.
- Description: Canonical fixed Net::CIDR::Lite issues that could bypass IP access control lists, a pbkdf2 issue that could generate predictable cryptographic keys, and an ldns issue that could allow spoofed DNS responses.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Ubuntu, and these are official Ubuntu package security notices published on June 18, 2026.
- Sources: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8453-1; https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8452-1; https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8449-1

**Finding 6: Google Chrome Stable security update, carried as Chromium exposure context**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: Chrome Stable 149.0.7827.155/.156 for Windows and Mac and 149.0.7827.155 for Linux, with 33 security fixes including Critical and High CVEs such as CVE-2026-12437 through CVE-2026-12469.
- Severity: Critical and High items are listed by Google.
- Description: Google’s Stable Channel update fixes multiple browser vulnerabilities, including use-after-free, heap buffer overflow, insufficient validation, and uninitialized-use issues.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Google Chrome. The Google release itself is dated June 16, slightly older than this run’s strict 24-hour window, but the related Chromium security fixes are relevant context for the June 18 Microsoft Edge Chromium update.
- Source: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/06/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_01750511403.html

**Possible matches needing review**

- Product: MongoDB / MongoDB Server
- Issue: CVE-2026-9740 and CVE-2026-11933, plus several lower-scored MongoDB Server CVEs including CVE-2026-9753, CVE-2026-9752, CVE-2026-9751, CVE-2026-9750, CVE-2026-9749, CVE-2026-9748, CVE-2026-9747, CVE-2026-9746, CVE-2026-9743, and CVE-2026-9741.
- Severity: Percona describes CVE-2026-9740 and CVE-2026-11933 as High; NVD records for some related MongoDB CVEs show MongoDB CNA CVSS values such as High under CVSS 4.0 and Medium under CVSS 3.1.
- Why review is needed: Percona published a fresh June 17 write-up saying the two high-severity issues affect MongoDB Community and Percona Server for MongoDB, and NVD enriched some MongoDB CVE records on June 18. However, the NVD records I checked show original CVE publication dates from June 9, so this is not being treated as a newly disclosed MongoDB finding without confirmation from MongoDB’s own advisory timeline.
- Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/security-advisory-cve-2026-9740-and-cve-2026-11933-in-percona-server-for-mongodb/; https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9752; https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9746

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Node.js supported release lines, Edge/Chromium browser exposure, and Ubuntu systems using the named packages, especially Tomcat and libheif. MongoDB should be reviewed against deployed versions and the official MongoDB advisory/release history before escalation.
